title: A class with private state
description:
Write a class `Inventory` that keeps item counts:

```javascript
const inv = new Inventory();
inv.add("apple", 3).add("pear").add("apple", 2);   // add(name, count = 1) returns this
inv.remove("apple", 4);                            // returns true; false (and no change) if there are not enough
inv.count("apple");                                // 1; 0 for unknown items
inv.total;                                         // a getter: the sum of all counts (2 here)
inv.names();                                       // names with a count above 0, sorted
Inventory.from({ tea: 2, cake: 1 });               // a static factory building an Inventory from an object
```

- The counts are stored in a **private** field, so `inv.items` and similar do not exist.
- `add` and `remove` throw a `RangeError` when `count` is not a positive whole number.
- An item whose count reaches 0 is removed completely.

Then write `class LimitedInventory extends Inventory`, built with `new LimitedInventory(max)`, whose `add` throws a `RangeError` with the message `full` when the total would go above `max`; otherwise it adds as usual.
hints: `#counts = new Map();` as a field gives every instance its own private Map. Methods can be private too: `#checkCount(count) { ... }`.
In the subclass, check the limit first and then call `super.add(name, count)` so the parent's checks and storage still run.
